intelligence.enrichment: A solid keeps its shape, a liquid flows and takes the shape of its container while keeping its volume, and a gas spreads through the available space without a fixed shape. The state of a substance determines whether it keeps shape, flows, or spreads through space. The learner correctly applies this rule: A solid keeps its shape, a liquid flows and takes the shape of its container while keeping its volume, and a gas spreads through the available space without a fixed shape. Shape alone tells the state; if something has any shape at the moment, it is solid.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Science question. Chapter: A journey through states of water. The student must decide: Decide whether a sample is behaving as a solid, liquid, or gas based on shape, flow, and spreading. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part.options, not typed into part text.
